outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Text-to-Image Diffusion Models and the Finetuning Problem
outline.description: This chapter introduces the landscape of text-to-image diffusion models, their capabilities, and the fundamental challenge of adapting them to downstream tasks. It sets the stage for understanding why finetuning is needed and what properties an ideal finetuning method should have.
subtopics: Overview of text-to-image diffusion models (Stable Diffusion, DALL-E, Imagen)
The two downstream tasks: subject-driven generation and controllable generation
Desiderata for effective finetuning: training efficiency and generalizability preservation
Limitations of existing finetuning strategies (small learning rate, low-rank re-parameterization)
The problem with Euclidean distance as a measure of semantic preservation
Motivation for a structural measure of model difference

outline.chapter_title: Neuron Angular Information and Semantic Representation
outline.description: This chapter explores the key insight that drives the OFT method: neuron directions (angles) encode semantic information. Through illustrative examples and experiments, students learn why modifying neuron directions is more effective for semantic adaptation than modifying magnitudes.
subtopics: Hyperspherical similarity and its role in encoding semantic information
Evidence from prior work: SphereNet and angular feature differences
Toy experiment: convolutional autoencoder demonstrating angular vs. magnitude information
Inspiration from 2D Fourier transform: phase spectrum preserves semantics
Implications for finetuning: why changing neuron directions is the key to semantic modification
The challenge of constraining the degree of freedom when modifying neuron directions

outline.chapter_title: Hyperspherical Energy: A Structural Measure of Neuron Relationships
outline.description: This chapter introduces hyperspherical energy as a mathematical tool to characterize the pairwise relational structure among neurons. Students learn how this measure captures neuron uniformity on the unit hypersphere and why preserving it is crucial for maintaining pretrained generative performance.
subtopics: Definition of hyperspherical energy and its computation
Pairwise neuron similarity on the unit hypersphere
Connection between hyperspherical energy and neuron uniformity
Hypothesis: minimal hyperspherical energy difference indicates better semantic preservation
Why a naive regularizer approach is insufficient
The invariance property: orthogonal transformations preserve pairwise hyperspherical similarity

outline.description: This chapter presents the core OFT method. Students learn how orthogonal transformations can provably preserve hyperspherical energy while adapting the model to downstream tasks, and understand the mathematical formulation of the OFT principle.
subtopics: From hyperspherical energy preservation to orthogonal transformation
Mathematical formulation of the OFT optimization problem
The layer-shared orthogonal transformation: R · W⁰
Identity initialization for starting from pretrained weights
Interpretation as adjusting the canonical coordinate system for neurons
Comparison to standard finetuning and LoRA constraints
OFT as a sweet spot between flexibility and regularity

outline.description: This chapter addresses the computational challenges of enforcing orthogonality. Students learn about the Cayley parameterization and block-diagonal structure that make OFT practical for large-scale diffusion models.
subtopics: Limitations of standard orthogonalization (Gram-Schmidt) for large matrices
Cayley parameterization: R = (I + Q)(I - Q)⁻¹ where Q is skew-symmetric
Properties and limitations of Cayley transform (special orthogonal group)
Block-diagonal orthogonal matrix structure for parameter efficiency
Parameter complexity analysis: O(d²/r) and O(d²/r²) with block sharing
Comparison of parameter efficiency between OFT and LoRA
Preservation of orthogonality under parameter-efficient strategies

outline.description: This chapter introduces COFT, an extension of OFT that adds an explicit radius constraint to improve finetuning stability. Students learn how the deviation constraint is incorporated and how it balances flexibility with stability.
subtopics: Motivation: combining hyperspherical energy preservation with deviation constraint
Mathematical formulation of COFT with ε-deviation constraint
Neumann series approximation of the Cayley transform
Translating the constraint on R to a constraint on Q
Projected gradient descent for enforcing the constraint
Effect of ε on finetuning flexibility and stability
Zero-initialization of Q for identity initialization of R

outline.description: This chapter covers a simple but effective extension of OFT that additionally learns magnitude scaling coefficients. Students also understand the broader applicability of OFT across different architectures.
subtopics: Motivation for re-scaled OFT: magnitude does not affect hyperspherical energy
Mathematical formulation: z = (R · W⁰ · D)⊤x with learnable diagonal matrix D
Additional flexibility with negligible parameter overhead
Architecture agnosticism: applying OFT to Transformers and CNNs
OFT for convolution layers: block-diagonal structure as depth-wise transformations
Block sharing across channels for parameter reduction

outline.chapter_title: Insights: Connections to LoRA, Convergence, and Design Principles
outline.description: This chapter provides deeper insights into why OFT works, its relationship to other methods, and the underlying principles that govern its behavior. Students gain intuition about the trade-offs in finetuning design.
subtopics: Rewriting OFT as a low-rank weight update analogous to LoRA
LoRA exploits low-rank structure vs. OFT exploits sparsity (block-diagonal) structure
Why OFT converges faster: effective semantic updates and smooth optimization landscape
Why not minimize hyperspherical energy: preserving vs. minimizing for finetuning
The flexibility-regularity trade-off in finetuning method design
No additional inference overhead: merging R into W⁰
Comparison to orthogonal over-parameterized training

outline.description: This chapter presents comprehensive experiments on subject-driven generation, comparing OFT and COFT to DreamBooth and LoRA. Students learn about evaluation metrics, convergence behavior, and qualitative differences.
subtopics: Experimental setup: Stable Diffusion v1.5, DreamBooth framework, baseline configurations
Finetuning stability and convergence analysis across iterations
Quantitative metrics: DINO, CLIP-I, CLIP-T, LPIPS for subject fidelity and diversity
Quantitative comparison results and statistical significance (30 random seeds)
Qualitative comparison: subject preservation and text prompt following
Robustness to hyperparameter settings (iteration count insensitivity)
Human evaluation of generation quality

outline.description: This chapter covers experiments on controllable generation tasks, including Canny edge-to-image, segmentation-to-image, and landmark-to-face. Students learn about the novel control consistency metric and how OFT outperforms existing methods.
subtopics: Task setup: C2I on COCO, S2I on ADE20K, L2F on CelebA-HQ
Baselines: ControlNet, T2I-Adapter, LoRA
Convergence analysis: faster and smoother convergence compared to baselines
Data efficiency: OFT converges with 5% of training data
Control consistency metric: estimating control signals from generated images
Quantitative comparison: IoU, F1, mean IoU, accuracy, ℓ₂ distance
Qualitative comparison across all three control tasks
Additional control tasks: dense pose, sketch, depth to image

outline.chapter_title: Conclusions, Open Problems, and Future Directions
outline.description: This chapter summarizes the key contributions of the OFT framework and discusses important open problems that remain to be addressed. Students reflect on the broader implications and potential extensions of the method.
subtopics: Summary of contributions: OFT, COFT, and empirical validation
Open problem 1: Scalability of Cayley parameterization and matrix inverse
Open problem 2: Compositionality of orthogonal matrices from multiple tasks
Open problem 3: Parameter efficiency and bias in block-diagonal structure
Broader implications for finetuning large generative models
Potential applications beyond text-to-image generation
